evidence_labels.VERIFIED: Confirmed from an identified official/authoritative source or publisher documentation.
evidence_labels.MEASURED: Exact source data were queried/downloaded and joined to stable_supported_v1.
evidence_labels.ESTIMATED: Preliminary Phase 3C judgement; not an exhaustive coverage or licensing audit.

measurement_note: Only C53 coverage is measured. All other stable-91 statements are preliminary estimates based on publisher scope.

recurring_families.note: CC BY 4.0 national/global datasets; only C53 has measured stable-91 coverage.
Strong harmonised public-service definitions; quality, self-reporting and local granularity differ.
Broad scope and favourable reuse; exact current bulk files still need probes.
Useful global scope but require overlap, uncertainty and component-selection controls.
Conceptually relevant but constrained by coverage, mixed field years and/or reuse rights.
Authoritative but unsuitable for unrestricted production reuse under identified licences.

city_level_treatment.reason: Reliability is utility/network and neighbourhood specific.
National basic-service access hides local quality and network gaps.
Gridded hazards should eventually be population/city weighted.
National hazard risk hides flood, wildfire, cyclone and seismic zones.
Environmental exposure is local, while the candidate is a licence-blocked national composite.

batch_conclusion: Batch 3 adds one deterministic Phase 3E candidate (C53) and eight conditional experimental candidates. It does not justify a fourth broad Phase 3C batch; consolidate all batches in Phase 3E.

criteria.name: Water quality and sanitation
criteria.question: How widely can residents rely on at least basic drinking-water and sanitation services in the destination country?
criteria.definition: Narrow to the lower of population shares using at least basic drinking-water and at least basic sanitation services. Do not label this tap-water safety or continuity.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: 86/91 measured (94.5%) for both basic components with a 2022-2024 observation
coverage.source_scope: JMP 2025 reports basic drinking water for 217 countries/areas and basic sanitation for 210
coverage.rationale: The exact WDI/JMP API intersection clears the 82-country threshold. Safely managed water plus sanitation reaches only 66/91.

sources.publisher: WHO/UNICEF JMP via World Bank WDI

methodology: JMP applies harmonised service ladders to household survey, census and administrative inputs.
Basic service is not equivalent to contaminant-free, continuously available household tap water.
licensing: World Bank-distributed WDI data are CC BY 4.0; pin exact indicator metadata and attribution.
WHO/UNICEF source attribution should be retained.
mapping: Five stable-universe countries lack one or both fresh basic-service components.
National averages obscure city, neighbourhood and network differences.

scoring.transformation: Use min(basic water %, basic sanitation %), winsorised only if necessary; expose both components.

limitations: Weak proxy for water quality in high-income destinations.
Country estimates may be modelled and lag local infrastructure changes.
criteria.recommendation: Proceed to Phase 3E with the narrow basic-service definition and explicit missing-country outcomes; keep safely managed services as optional metadata.
open: Is a high-coverage but low-discrimination basic-service score valuable enough for relocation ranking?

evidence.claim: Exact WDI API join returned 86/91 fresh intersections.
The safely managed pair returned 66/91.

criteria.name: Work-life balance
criteria.question: How heavy is the average weekly working-time burden for employed people in the destination?
criteria.definition: Narrow to mean weekly hours actually worked per employed person; it does not measure leave, schedule control, commute or subjective balance.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 82/91 appears plausible; exact indicator download not joined
coverage.source_scope: ILOSTAT publishes global modelled estimates, November 2025 edition
coverage.rationale: Modelled global scope is promising, but exact stable-91 recency and sex/age aggregates remain unmeasured.

sources.series_or_table: Average weekly hours actually worked per employed person by sex — ILO modelled estimates, Nov. 2025

methodology: Actual hours exclude annual leave, public holidays, sickness, parental leave and commuting.
Modelled estimates improve coverage but depend on harmonisation and imputation.
licensing: ILO open data published after 3 May 2023 are generally CC BY 4.0; capture the exact bulk-file notice.
mapping: National ISO mapping should be tractable; aggregation and observation-status fields must be retained.

scoring.transformation: Reverse robust percentile of mean weekly hours; label as working-time burden.

limitations: Cannot substantiate the broad work-life-balance label.
Informal work and multiple jobs may be measured unevenly.
criteria.recommendation: Run an experimental Phase 3E probe only after renaming to Working-time burden.
open: Should paid leave be a separate policy/profile feature rather than folded into this score?

evidence.claim: ILOSTAT lists a November 2025 modelled average-weekly-hours table.
Stable-91 coverage has not been measured.

criteria.name: Social protection and welfare support
criteria.question: What share of residents is effectively covered by at least one social-protection benefit?
criteria.definition: Narrow to effective social-protection coverage; it does not establish a new immigrant's eligibility, adequacy or waiting period.
criteria.observation: Administrative reports plus ILO modelled estimates

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 90% appears highly plausible; exact stable-91 join not performed
coverage.source_scope: ILO model output supplies complete 2009-2023 series for 189 countries/territories
coverage.rationale: Publisher scope clears the threshold, but reported versus imputed values must be distinguished.

sources.dataset: World Social Protection Database / WSPR 2024-26 annex

methodology: The complete series includes reported and imputed observations.
Coverage says whether a benefit is received, not its value or migrant eligibility.
licensing: ILO terms are favourable, but the exact downloadable database asset and attribution must be pinned.
mapping: Country mapping should be broad; preserve imputation flags and benefit-population definitions.

scoring.transformation: Published effective-coverage percentage; report imputation and do not infer newcomer entitlement.

limitations: Legal residents, temporary migrants and citizens can face different entitlements.
High coverage may coexist with low benefit adequacy.
criteria.recommendation: Run a conditional Phase 3E probe as a national welfare-system reach proxy.
open: Should imputed observations receive lower confidence or remain unscored?

evidence.claim: ILO states that model output provides complete 2009-2023 series for 189 countries and territories.
Stable-91 coverage is publisher-scope based, not measured.

criteria.name: Food safety and public-health protection
criteria.question: How strong is the country's self-reported capacity to prevent, detect and respond to food-safety and wider public-health threats?
criteria.definition: Use WHO SPAR Food Safety capacity (C13) as a narrow system-capacity proxy, not observed foodborne-illness risk.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 82/91 appears highly plausible; exact 2025 download not joined
coverage.source_scope: WHO SPAR covers IHR States Parties using 35 indicators across 15 capacities
coverage.rationale: Annual global reporting is broad, but non-response and self-assessment bias need measurement.

sources.dataset: State Party Self-Assessment Annual Reporting Tool (SPAR)

methodology: SPAR is a structured annual self-assessment against IHR capacities.
It measures national capacity, not inspections, outbreak incidence or restaurant-level safety.
licensing: WHO data terms generally use CC BY 4.0 with dataset-specific notices; verify the dashboard export.
mapping: States Parties map nationally; preserve missing reports and score revisions.

scoring.transformation: Use published C13 capacity score only; avoid averaging all 15 IHR capacities.

limitations: Self-reporting may inflate capacity.
National capacity may not predict day-to-day food safety.
criteria.recommendation: Run an experimental Phase 3E probe; label it Food-safety system capacity.
open: Is a system-capacity measure sufficiently decision-useful without outcome data?

evidence.claim: WHO exposes a 2025 SPAR capacity dashboard including Food Safety.
Stable-91 coverage is not measured.

criteria.name: Long-term climate-change exposure
criteria.question: How large are projected long-term heat and precipitation changes under a declared emissions scenario and horizon?
criteria.definition: A scenario-specific national climate-hazard projection, not a single factual forecast or vulnerability score.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: 91/91 spatial coverage appears plausible; country aggregation not measured
coverage.source_scope: World Bank CCKP CMIP6 is global at 0.25 degrees, 1950-2100
coverage.rationale: Raster coverage is global, but a defensible national aggregation and coastal/territory mapping must be tested.

sources.publisher: World Bank Climate Change Knowledge Portal
sources.series_or_table: Temperature and precipitation projections by SSP/horizon

methodology: Results depend on scenario, reference period, horizon, ensemble statistic and variable.
Country means can hide populated-coast and city exposure.
licensing: The World Bank catalogue marks the dataset CC BY 4.0.
mapping: Requires reproducible country geometry and land/population weighting.
Small islands may need careful grid-cell treatment.

scoring.transformation: No single score until scenario, horizon, variables and weighting are user-approved.

limitations: Projection uncertainty is material.
Hazard change is not adaptation capacity or realised loss.
criteria.recommendation: Run an experimental methodology probe, not a production score probe.
open: Which SSP, horizon and exposure variables answer the relocation question?

evidence.claim: CCKP provides global 0.25-degree CMIP6 data through 2100 under CC BY 4.0.
Stable-91 country aggregation was not measured.

criteria.name: Digital-government readiness
criteria.question: How extensively has the government adopted common digital-government systems and practices?
criteria.definition: Use GovTech practices/components diagnostically; do not represent GTMI as an official readiness ranking.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: About 90/91 appears plausible; Nicaragua is the known publisher-scope exclusion
coverage.source_scope: 2025 GovTech dataset covers 197 economies; 158 survey responses and 39 public-data assessments
coverage.rationale: Publisher scope is nearly complete but the exact workbook was not joined.

methodology: The World Bank explicitly says GTMI is not intended to rank or assess readiness/performance.
Mixed self-reported and public-web inputs can have different evidence quality.
licensing: The dataset catalogue specifies CC BY 4.0.
mapping: Economy-to-ISO mapping should be strong; Nicaragua requires explicit missing handling.

scoring.transformation: Use component facts or an unscored diagnostic until a defensible relocation-oriented construct exists.

limitations: Practice adoption does not prove service usability for immigrants.
Triennial updates are adequate only for structural change.
criteria.recommendation: Experimental only; inspect components in Phase 3E and reject a direct GTMI rank.
open: Which GovTech components directly affect a newcomer rather than general public administration?

evidence.claim: The 2025 dataset covers 197 economies and is CC BY 4.0.
The publisher says GTMI is not a readiness/performance ranking.

criteria.name: Natural-disaster risk
criteria.question: How exposed is the destination to natural hazards after accounting for vulnerability and coping capacity?
criteria.definition: Use INFORM Risk or its natural-hazard components; separate hazard exposure from vulnerability/governance.
criteria.observation: Composite of hazard, exposure, vulnerability and coping indicators

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 90% appears plausible; exact release join not measured
coverage.source_scope: INFORM is a global open-source risk assessment
coverage.rationale: Global scope appears sufficient but the exact downloadable release and stable join remain to be pinned.

sources.publisher: European Commission JRC and INFORM partners
sources.series_or_table: Natural hazard/exposure, vulnerability, lack of coping capacity

methodology: Composite structure is transparent, but broad vulnerability and coping inputs overlap governance and development criteria.
The full risk score is not a pure natural-hazard exposure measure.
licensing: The project is open-source, but exact dataset-asset reuse terms require capture before redistribution.
mapping: Country scope is global; conflict/territory treatment and missing-component imputation require inspection.

scoring.transformation: Prefer published natural-hazard/exposure dimension; test against full INFORM score.

limitations: National scores obscure local hazard zones.
Shared governance inputs could double count.
criteria.recommendation: Conditional Phase 3E probe focused on natural-hazard exposure, subject to exact licence capture.
open: Use exposure-only or the full vulnerability-adjusted risk score?

evidence.claim: INFORM documents a global composite of hazards/exposure, vulnerability and lack of coping capacity.
Exact stable-91 coverage and asset licence were not measured.

criteria.name: International-student accessibility
criteria.question: How established is the destination as a host for internationally mobile tertiary students?
criteria.definition: Narrow to inbound internationally mobile student stock/rate; it measures realised presence, not admission, visa, tuition or accessibility.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 82/91 appears plausible; exact series join not measured
coverage.source_scope: UNESCO UIS releases cover more than 200 countries and territories
coverage.rationale: Publisher scope is broad, but inbound-mobility availability and recency vary.

sources.series_or_table: Inbound internationally mobile students; inbound mobility rate

methodology: Internationally mobile students are identified by prior residence or education where available.
Observed inbound stock reflects attractiveness and capacity as well as accessibility.
licensing: Exact UIS bulk-download licence and third-party restrictions need capture; do not infer from general UNESCO pages.
mapping: Country/economy and academic-year mapping need normalization.
Very small destinations can have volatile rates.

scoring.transformation: Prefer published inbound mobility rate; do not call it admissions accessibility.

limitations: Does not measure tuition, visas, language or selectivity.
May reward destinations with capacity constraints and high fees.
criteria.recommendation: Experimental only after renaming to International-student presence; otherwise defer.
open: Is realised student presence a useful independent criterion or only context for C01/C35?

evidence.claim: UIS states that its 2025 education release covers more than 200 countries and territories.
Exact stable-91 coverage and licence were not measured.

criteria.name: Religious freedom and freedom of expression
criteria.question: How strongly are freedom of expression and religious freedom protected in law and practice?
criteria.definition: Use a small, predeclared V-Dem indicator/index subset with uncertainty; do not invent a broad civil-liberties composite.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: At least 90% appears plausible; exact variables not joined
coverage.source_scope: V-Dem v16 contains country-year data for 531 indicators and 251 indices
coverage.rationale: Dataset scope is broad, but exact variables, rater counts and current values require a probe.

sources.series_or_table: Freedom of expression and religion-related indicators/indices

methodology: Expert-coded estimates include uncertainty and variable rater counts.
V-Dem recommends caution or filtering when an observation has three or fewer raters.
licensing: V-Dem says its data are open source and free to use, but an exact commercial redistribution licence was not verified for the v16 archive.
mapping: Historical country units and current states require a pinned country-year mapping.
Retain uncertainty and rater-count variables.

scoring.transformation: Select published indices or variables; use latest multi-year median and expose uncertainty.

limitations: Expert perception may not represent minority-specific lived experience.
Combining two freedoms introduces normative weighting.
criteria.recommendation: Conditional experimental probe only after exact licence and variable selection are resolved.
open: Separate expression and religion into preference-weighted dimensions?
Which v16 variables have adequate rater counts?

evidence.claim: V-Dem v16 was released in March 2026 and provides 531 indicators and 251 indices.
Commercial redistribution terms for the exact v16 archive remain unverified.

criteria.name: Climate resilience and adaptation readiness
criteria.question: How ready is a country to convert investment into climate adaptation while reducing vulnerability?
criteria.definition: ND-GAIN readiness/vulnerability composite, with overlap explicitly audited.

coverage.source_scope: ND-GAIN download page states 192 UN countries with data through 2024
coverage.rationale: Coverage is strong, but the reason to defer is construct overlap rather than country availability.

methodology: Readiness includes economic, governance and social inputs; vulnerability spans six sectors.
Many inputs overlap governance, innovation, education, infrastructure and ICT criteria.
licensing: Download page specifies CC Attribution 3.0 Unported.
mapping: Broad UN-country coverage; exact current download should be joined if revived.

scoring.transformation: Published score only; no Konsider reweighting without overlap analysis.

limitations: Composite score obscures drivers.
Current pages contain inconsistent historical-period wording.
criteria.recommendation: Defer until the active catalog is consolidated in Phase 3E; revive only if it replaces rather than duplicates multiple criteria.
open: Would ND-GAIN replace C67/C68 plus governance inputs, or is hazard-specific scoring preferable?

evidence.claim: ND-GAIN states coverage of 192 UN countries and CC BY 3.0 reuse.
Overlap judgement is preliminary.

criteria.name: Overall life satisfaction
criteria.question: How do residents rate their lives overall in the destination?
criteria.definition: Country-level Cantril Ladder life evaluation, typically reported as a three-year average.

coverage.stable_91_estimate: Likely below full coverage and potentially near the threshold; not measured
coverage.source_scope: World Happiness Report 2026 publishes country three-year averages using Gallup World Poll
coverage.rationale: Small states and irregular survey years may create gaps.

sources.publisher: Wellbeing Research Centre / Gallup / UN SDSN

methodology: Life evaluation is a standard 0-10 Cantril Ladder measure.
Three-year pooling improves precision but reduces freshness and can straddle shocks.
licensing: Underlying Gallup World Poll microdata and extended data require institutional access; exact commercial reuse of report tables is unresolved.
mapping: Some small countries lack recent observations; country labels require a join.

scoring.transformation: Published three-year average if licensed; retain confidence intervals.

limitations: Broad outcome can double-count all domain-specific criteria.
Respondent adaptation and culture affect comparisons.
criteria.recommendation: Defer pending exact dataset licence and overlap policy.
open: Should subjective wellbeing be an independent outcome or a validation benchmark?

evidence.claim: WHR 2026 publishes three-year life-evaluation averages based on Gallup World Poll.
Stable-91 coverage and production licence are unverified.

criteria.name: Social inclusion and acceptance of immigrants
criteria.question: How accepting are residents of immigrants as neighbours or members of society?
criteria.definition: A repeated national-attitude measure; WVS is the best open research candidate but not a current global production panel.

coverage.rationale: Publisher scope alone is below the 90% threshold and observations are mixed-date.

sources.series_or_table: Immigrants/foreign workers as neighbours and related attitudes

methodology: National probability samples are typically 1,000-3,200 respondents.
Question wording and social desirability limit interpretation as lived immigrant experience.
licensing: Data are free for academic use; production/commercial redistribution terms require explicit permission.
mapping: Wave coverage and field years vary; societies and territories need normalization.

scoring.transformation: Possible percentage rejecting anti-immigrant response, but not production-ready.

limitations: Below threshold and stale for fast-moving sentiment.
Attitudes do not measure discrimination outcomes.
criteria.recommendation: Defer; revisit only with a licensed recurring global attitude source.
open: Would a smaller-country experimental layer be useful despite missingness?

evidence.claim: WVS Wave 7 reports 77 participating countries/societies and 2017-2021 fieldwork.
Stable-91 coverage is inferred from publisher scope, not joined.

criteria.name: Water-supply reliability
criteria.question: Can households in likely destination cities obtain safe piped water continuously when needed?
criteria.definition: Utility/city continuity and service-interruption performance, not national basic-water access.
criteria.observation: Household survey or utility administrative data

coverage.stable_91_estimate: Below 82/91 for the exact reliability construct is likely
coverage.source_scope: JMP 2025 reports 'available when needed' for 144 countries/areas globally
coverage.rationale: Global publisher scope does not ensure stable-universe coverage, and high-income reporting is incomplete.

methodology: Availability when needed is one safely managed service component.
Household responses do not provide utility outage frequency or neighbourhood reliability.
licensing: JMP reuse terms and exact downloadable-file notices require capture.
mapping: Utility boundaries rarely align with national or city boundaries.
National estimates can conceal rationing in particular cities.

scoring.transformation: No independent national score; future city layer could use hours/day and interruption frequency.

limitations: Coverage below threshold is likely.
Exact relocation value is city and neighbourhood specific.
criteria.recommendation: Defer to a city/utility data programme and keep C53 as the national service proxy.
open: Which priority cities and utility metrics should define a later pilot?

evidence.claim: JMP 2025 reports availability-when-needed estimates for 144 countries/areas.
Stable-91 coverage was not joined.

criteria.name: LGBTQ+ legal and social inclusion
criteria.question: How inclusive is the destination's law for LGBTQ+ people?
criteria.definition: ILGA World legal-category evidence; social inclusion would require a separate survey source.

coverage.source_scope: ILGA World Laws on Us tracks 11 legal categories globally
coverage.rationale: Coverage is not the blocker; reuse terms are.

methodology: Legal categories are comparable but do not capture social acceptance, enforcement or subnational variation.
licensing: The current report page states CC BY-NC 4.0, incompatible with an unrestricted commercial production dataset.
A conflicting asset snippet makes conservative treatment necessary; obtain written permission before reconsideration.
mapping: National legal mapping is broad; federal/subnational exceptions may matter.

scoring.transformation: Technically possible but normatively weighted and presently licence-blocked.

limitations: Law is not lived inclusion.
Combining 11 categories requires normative choices.
criteria.recommendation: Reject for Phase 3E production candidacy unless ILGA grants suitable reuse permission.
open: Would ILGA provide a commercial licence or written permission for derived country scores?

evidence.claim: The ILGA report page states CC BY-NC 4.0.
Global coverage was not joined because licence is dispositive.

criteria.name: Environmental quality beyond PM2.5
criteria.question: How well does the country perform across environmental health and ecosystem vitality beyond air pollution?
criteria.observation: Composite of modelled and reported indicators

sources.publisher: Yale Center for Environmental Law & Policy

methodology: Methodology and indicators change between editions; Yale warns against comparing scores across editions.
The composite overlaps air, climate, water, biodiversity and sanitation criteria.
licensing: EPI 2024 is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and prohibits commercial use.
mapping: National mapping is broad but does not solve city-level environmental variation.

scoring.transformation: Do not ingest or rescore under current licence.

limitations: Composite is broad and version-unstable.
National score hides local exposures.
criteria.recommendation: Reject as an independent production criterion; use open, specific indicators instead.
open: None unless commercial permission becomes available.

evidence.claim: Yale states EPI 2024 is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and editions are not directly comparable.
